title: SysPilot: Cross-Library Performance Autotuning via Library Performance Contracts
abstract: arXiv:2611.06078v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Modern scientific and machine-learning applications compose many independently developed libraries. When these libraries run together, their independently managed runtimes can oversubscribe shared resources: using the same CPU cores, fighting over GPUs, or contending for memory bandwidth. Avoiding such contention requires careful configuration across library boundaries. Existing autotuners do not directly investigate what resources are shared between libraries, which runtime signals correlate with interference. As a result, they are inefficient for finding optimal configurations to mitigate contention.   This paper presents SysPilot, a cross-library performance autotuning system based on Library Performance Contract (LPC). A Library Performance Contract captures a library's resource demands, assumptions, controls, and observability signals in LPCL, a specification language for describing library resource requirements. translated_title: SysPilot：基于库性能契约的跨库性能自动调优
translated_abstract: 现代科学计算与机器学习应用由许多独立开发的库组合而成。当这些库共同运行时，它们各自独立管理的运行时可能会过度占用共享资源：使用相同的CPU核心、争夺GPU，或竞争内存带宽。要避免此类资源争用，需要跨库边界进行细致的配置。现有的自动调优工具并不会直接探究库之间共享了哪些资源、哪些运行时信号与干扰相关，因此在寻找缓解争用的最优配置方面效率低下。本文提出了SysPilot，一个基于库性能契约的跨库性能自动调优系统。库性能契约通过LPCL——一种用于描述库资源需求的规格说明语言——来刻画库的资源需求、假设条件、控制项以及可观测性信号。SysPilot综合
tldr: SysPilot提出“库性能契约”机制，通过规格化语言描述各库的资源需求与可观测信号，实现跨库性能自动调优，有效缓解多个独立库共同运行时的共享资源争用问题。
en_tdlr: SysPilot introduces Library Performance Contracts (LPC), a specification-based approach to capture each library's resource demands and runtime signals, enabling cross-library performance autotuning that effectively mitigates shared-resource contention among independently developed libraries.
